tasks.short: Plan training sessions around rooms, forklifts, instructors and shift rosters, then book and enrol people.

steps.what: Collect who needs which course: expiring certificates, new starters, requests
Check room, training equipment and instructor availability per site
Match slots to shift rosters and agree release of staff with team leads
Create sessions, enrol learners, send invites to staff and instructors
Handle cancellations, no-shows and rebookings

tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform reads Studytube expiry dates and enrolments, AFAS employee and site data, the shift roster and Outlook resource calendars for rooms, forklifts and instructors, and proposes a session plan per site. The L&D specialist approves or edits it in a small planning app; approved sessions are created in Studytube with Outlook invites, and team leads get a notice of who is released when. No model is needed at run time.
tasks.previous_blocker: The data sat in three places (Studytube, AFAS, team-lead rosters) and nobody would fund custom integration for a 140-hour-a-year task.
tasks.enabler_now: Studytube and AFAS have APIs and AI-assisted coding makes a small scheduler and approval screen a matter of days, not a project.
tasks.still_hard: Shift rosters may live outside AFAS or in team-lead spreadsheets, and external VCA and forklift instructors confirm by mail, so their availability stays partly manual.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiating release of shift staff in peak season with team leads, and judging which lapse risk matters most when slots are scarce.

ambition.what: Re-plan certificate sessions weekly per site instead of quarterly, so no shift worker starts a shift with a lapsed forklift or VCA certificate.

tasks.altitude: The specialist stops building the schedule and approves a proposed plan in about 30 minutes a week; they gain the right to book shift staff for training within agreed release windows.

reach.task: Maintaining employee site and function data in AFAS
reach.learn: Which AFAS fields drive enrolment rules, so wrong data does not cause missed certificates.

reach.task: Running the nightly AFAS extract and Power BI dashboards
reach.learn: How to add a certificate-coverage measure per site and shift to the existing data model.

evidence.claim: Studytube is the LMS holding courses, enrolments and mandatory certificate expiry dates.
Certificate expiry, enrolment and scheduling suit deterministic software combining Studytube expiry dates and AFAS rosters.
Outside bodies certify VCA and forklift skills; the scheduler only books training and exams.

assumptions: Shift rosters are available digitally per site, in AFAS or an export.
Rooms and training equipment can be set up as Outlook resource mailboxes.
About 138 hours a year across the 2 FTE go to this task.
unknowns: Where shift rosters are kept and whether they have an API or export.
How many external training providers deliver certificate courses and how they confirm dates.
Whether the works council sees combined roster and training data as a monitoring-capable tool (WOR 27(1)(l)).
research_questions: How many certificate lapses per site occurred last year, and how many were caused by scheduling rather than no-shows?
Can the Studytube API create classroom sessions and enrolments, or only read them?
What share of rescheduling is caused by roster changes after booking?

tasks.short: Track training spend against budget and write reports that justify the cost to HR and finance.

steps.what: Collect training invoices, licence costs and course fees
Allocate costs to site, department, course type and learners

loop.input: Invoice lines with free-text descriptions that do not match a course code
loop.output: Proposed course code, site and cost centre with a confidence flag
loop.check: Amounts must reconcile to the ledger total; codes must exist in the course list; low-confidence lines go to review
loop.stop: One pass per line; unmatched or low-confidence lines go to the specialist's review queue
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier invoices describe courses in free text that differs per provider; rules cover most but not all lines.

steps.what: Compare spend to budget and spot overruns
Write the budget report explaining spend and outcomes

loop.input: Variance table, certificate coverage and onboarding figures for the period
loop.output: Draft narrative of two to three paragraphs per section
loop.check: Every number in the text is matched against the source table by code; mismatches block the draft
loop.stop: Up to two redrafts; then the specialist writes the section
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template covers the tables, but the explanation of why spend moved needs written text that changes each period.

steps.what: Discuss the report with the HR director and controller

tasks.design: Replace the training-cost Excel file with a nightly job on the governed data platform that pulls training-related invoices and ledger lines from AFAS and enrolments from Studytube, allocates them by rules plus a small classification loop for unclear invoice lines, and feeds a Power BI training-spend page next to the existing HR dashboards. Each quarter a generator drafts the budget report from the same tables; the specialist edits it and the controller sees the same numbers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training invoices are booked on generic cost accounts in AFAS and supplier descriptions do not match course names, so matching took manual work every month.
tasks.enabler_now: The nightly AFAS extract already exists for Power BI, and a bounded model step can now map free-text invoice lines to course codes with a reconciliation check.
tasks.still_hard: Spend that is not invoiced (internal instructor hours, lost shift hours) and sector training fund subsidies need agreed rules with finance before they can be counted.
tasks.human_edge: Arguing the case for training spend to the HR director and controller, and choosing which outcomes (certified first shift, 90-day retention) to tie the money to.

ambition.what: A monthly training-spend view per site that the HR director and controller use to move budget between sites mid-year, instead of one year-end justification.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends an hour a month checking allocations and a few hours a quarter on the narrative; they gain a shared number with finance and a say in budget reallocation during the year.

reach.task: Booking supplier invoices in AFAS accounts payable
reach.learn: How a training cost centre or course code on the invoice at booking would remove most matching work.

reach.task: Preparing the yearly budget and forecasts
reach.learn: How finance builds the training budget line so L&D reports in the same structure.

evidence.claim: Power BI dashboards run on a nightly AFAS extract at Noordhaven, a base for a training-spend page.
Workday advises measuring baselines before launching AI in HR workflows.
No published case shows a course cutting time-to-skill, so reports should tie spend to certification and retention rather than claimed learning gains.

assumptions: Training invoices go through AFAS accounts payable.
A training budget per site or department exists in AFAS or Excel.
About 132 hours a year across the 2 FTE go to this task.
unknowns: Which ledger accounts and cost centres hold training spend today.
Whether Noordhaven claims sector training fund or STAP-like subsidies and how they are booked.
Whether per-person cost allocation is allowed under the works council agreement on personal data.
research_questions: What share of training invoice lines can be matched to a course by supplier and amount rules alone?
Does the controller accept a model-assisted allocation with a review queue as the basis for the budget line?
Which outcome measures does the HR director want next to spend in the report?

tasks.short: Design and run development programmes that grow warehouse and office staff into team lead and management roles.

steps.what: Identify needs and candidates with HR business partners and managers
Design the programme: modules, mentoring, job rotations, timing

loop.input: Development needs, competence profile for the target role, existing Studytube catalogue
loop.output: Draft programme outline with module list and reuse of existing courses
loop.check: Specialist reviews; every module must map to a competence in the profile
loop.stop: One draft plus up to two revisions per request; then manual design
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning loose needs into a structured outline is writing work; a template alone gives empty boxes.

steps.what: Build materials: cases, workshop scripts, e-learning modules
Run sessions, coaching and mentor matching
Track progress and evaluate the programme at group level

loop.output: Themes with counts at group level
loop.check: Specialist reads a sample per theme; no individual scores, never fed into appraisals
loop.stop: One clustering pass per evaluation round; groups under five people are not reported
loop.why_not_simpler: Open comments cannot be counted by rules; the rest (attendance, promotions, retention) is plain reporting.

tasks.design: Keep selection and delivery human. Use Studytube AI Authoring and a drafting step in Microsoft 365 to produce programme outlines and modules from the competence profile, and a Power BI page that follows participants' completion, promotion and retention at group level with a comment-clustering step for feedback. A feedback-practice copilot can support new team leads, disclosed as AI.
tasks.previous_blocker: Programmes were built from scratch each time and the specialist had little time beside scheduling and compliance training, so floor staff rarely got a development track.
tasks.enabler_now: Studytube's authoring feature drafts modules from uploaded material, freeing design time, and drafting tools make outlines quick to produce and revise.
tasks.still_hard: Picking candidates fairly across sites and shifts, and showing results, which only appear after months. Any AI that scores candidates would be high-risk under the AI Act from December 2027 and needs works council consent.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting potential in people on the floor, convincing managers to release them, and coaching them through the first lead role.

ambition.what: A team-lead track for warehouse and transport shift workers on all three sites, including night shifts, who have had no development route so far.

tasks.altitude: Less time on slide building, more time with candidates and managers; the specialist gets a recognised voice in succession talks with HR business partners.

reach.task: Succession and talent reviews with site managers
reach.learn: How managers judge readiness for a lead role, to shape programme content.
How to follow programme participants' promotion and 90-day retention in a new role without individual profiling.

evidence.claim: Studytube AI Authoring drafts outlines, scripts and questions from a title or uploaded file; authors edit.
A feedback check-in agent drafting against the SBI rubric raised write-up quality more for users (16 points) than non-users (7).
Microsoft's learning agent shows skill gaps and pathways while HR still guides role moves and leadership development.
AI using learning data to evaluate workers is high-risk from 2 December 2027.

assumptions: Competence profiles for team lead and shift manager roles exist or can be written.
About 116 hours a year across the 2 FTE go to this task.
unknowns: Whether a formal succession list exists per site.
How many internal promotions to team lead happen each year.
Whether the works council has agreed training policy covering development programmes (WOR 27(1)(f)).
research_questions: How many team lead vacancies were filled externally last year that internal candidates could have filled?
Do promoted floor staff have different 90-day and one-year retention than external hires?
Would site managers release candidates for a programme during peak season?

tasks.short: Build and roll out training on energy, fuel, waste separation and recycling for warehouse, transport and office staff.

steps.what: Gather requirements and site rules with facility and safety leads
Draft content: e-learning, toolbox talk cards, posters, translations

loop.input: Site procedures and training brief; target languages
loop.output: Draft module, quiz questions, toolbox card and translated versions
loop.check: Specialist edits; the site lead signs off the facts; translations checked by a native-speaking colleague or team lead
loop.stop: One draft per module plus two revision rounds; otherwise manual
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning procedures into plain short lessons in several languages is writing work no template does.

steps.what: Get sign-off from the facility or safety lead per site
Assign the course to target groups and plan toolbox sessions
Measure completion and effect on waste, energy and fuel

tasks.design: Draft modules and toolbox cards in Studytube AI Authoring from the site procedures on SharePoint, with translated versions for non-Dutch-speaking shift and flex staff, and a SharePoint approval flow for the site lead's sign-off. Studytube audience rules fed by AFAS function and site enrol people automatically, and a Power BI page puts completion next to site waste and fuel figures at site level.
tasks.previous_blocker: Low priority and low frequency: producing multilingual content for a yearly topic cost more than it seemed worth, so it stayed a slide deck at a toolbox meeting.
tasks.enabler_now: AI authoring and translation make short multilingual modules cheap, and Studytube audience rules can enrol by function and site without manual lists.
tasks.still_hard: Showing an effect: waste and fuel figures may not be tracked per site or team, and behaviour change depends on site managers, not the course.
tasks.human_edge: Working with site leads to choose the few behaviours that matter on each site and making the toolbox talk land with drivers and warehouse staff.

ambition.what: Flex workers from the three staffing agencies get the site waste and energy instruction in their own language on their first shift.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends time with site leads and on measuring, not producing slides; little else changes for this yearly task.

reach.task: Onboarding flex workers and new starters
reach.learn: Where a short site instruction fits in the first-shift checklist.

reach.task: Reporting energy and fuel costs per site
reach.learn: Which site figures exist to measure the training's effect.

evidence.claim: Studytube AI Authoring drafts course outlines, scripts and questions from an uploaded PDF or PPT.
MHR's learning team has an agent draft content and check reading level, with a person reviewing.
Faster content production is the top expected AI benefit among L&D practitioners.

assumptions: Site environmental procedures exist in writing on SharePoint.
A sizeable share of shift and flex staff prefer a language other than Dutch.
About 54 hours a year across the 2 FTE go to this task.
unknowns: Which languages flex and shift workers speak and whether agencies already give environmental instruction.
Whether waste, energy and fuel data are recorded per site.
Whether flex workers can be given Studytube accounts under the agency contracts.
research_questions: Do site waste or fuel figures move after a toolbox round, compared with a site that has not had it yet?
Can Studytube AI Authoring produce usable versions in the main languages of the flex workforce?
Do site leads accept signing off AI-drafted content within a week?

role.altitude: The two specialists move from building schedules, spreadsheets and slides to owning the competence record for 1,200 staff and flex workers: who is certified for which shift, what it costs, and the AI Act Article 4 literacy measures file. They approve plans and drafts instead of making them, and spend more time with site leads, managers and candidates.
reach: hrbp: succession and talent reviews, to shape development programmes
people-analyst: the nightly AFAS extract and Power BI model, to add certificate coverage and training-spend measures
bookkeeper: booking training invoices in AFAS, so costs carry a course code from the start
hr-admin: flex worker and new-starter onboarding, so first-shift certificates and instructions are in place
skills_to_grow: Reading and checking data flows between Studytube, AFAS and Power BI
Editing and fact-checking AI-drafted course material, including translations
Measuring programmes against North Star inputs (certified first shift, onboarding in week one, 90-day retention) instead of completions
AI Act basics: Article 4 literacy measures, Article 50 disclosure, high-risk rules from December 2027, and works council consent under WOR 27
role.ambitious_version: L&D runs a live certificate-coverage plan per site and shift, so no warehouse worker or flex worker starts a shift without valid forklift, VCA or food safety certificates, while a team-lead track gives floor staff on all three sites a route to promotion, with spend and results visible to the HR director and controller monthly.
